test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 8 Sept 2022 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: The newer, younger deposits of the flood plains called ______ are renewed almost every year, and hence are fertile, thus being ideal for intensive agriculture.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Khadar.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

**Khadar**

__
 
• The lowlands, also known as **Nali or Naili**, are referred to as Khadir or Khadar. Flood-prone Khadar regions frequently contain remnants of former **riverbeds** that have been converted into agricultural land as a result of river changes. When wet, it becomes sticky and receptive to moisture.
 
• The Khadir formation is made of** fresh alluvial soil** that is very fertile and has a higher content of the river's new silt. It is added to with each flood cycle.
 
• The Khadir is also known as Nali in northern Haryana, where it is the abundant prairie tract that lies between the **Ghaggar river** and the southern limits of the **Saraswati canal depression.** The khadar map shows that these areas flood when it rains.
 
• It retains **moisture and becomes sticky **when wet. Khadir soil is made up of newly deposited alluvial soil with more **river fresh silt**. It is renewed with each flooding cycle and frequently produces a lot of fruit.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

**Tarai**

 
• **​​**The Tarai, also spelled **Terai,** is a region in the north of India and the** south of Nepal** that runs parallel to the lower **Himalayan ranges**. It stretches from the **Yamuna River** in the west to the **Brahmaputra River** in the east, and it was once marshland.
 
• The Tarai, which means **"moist land,"** is formed by a number of springs at its northern edge, forming numerous streams, including the important **Ghaghara River**, which intersects the Tarai and contributes to its marshy appearance.
 
• The marshlands, which were once plagued by **malaria**, have been reduced by drainage and cultivation. In the state of** West Bengal **and in **Bangladesh**, the eastern Tarai is referred to as the **Duars.**

**Bangar**

 
• **​South** of the Bhabar and Terai Plains are the Bhangar Plains. In contrast to the Bhabar Plains, which are unsuitable for agriculture due to the presence of sediments, the Bhangar Plains, which are **well-drained plains** in Northern India, are suitable for agriculture.
 
• In the Bhangar Plains, the **old alluvial soil** has little terraces that are elevated and patches of alkaline efflorescences, also known as **"usar,"** which makes some areas infertile.

**Bhabar**

 
• **​**In India's Kumaon, Bhabar or Bhabhar is a region south of the **Shivalik Hills** and the Lower Himalayas. It is home to some of Kumaon's largest cities, including **Haldwani and Ramnagar**, both in the **Nainital** District.
 
• It is the alluvial apron formed by sediments that were washed down from the Shivalik's along the** Indo-Gangetic Plain's** northern edge.
